title: Applied torque has no effect if CollisionShape2D is disabled
body:
### Tested versions

v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8]

### System information

Godot v4.3.stable - Windows 10.0.26100 - GLES3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6636) - AMD Ryzen 9 8945HS w/ Radeon 780M Graphics (16 Threads)

### Issue description

This is a duplicate of [#27413](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/27413#issue-425040250). The bug(?) is still present in version 4.3 stable, so I wanted to bring attention to it again. I have left [a comment on the original issue](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/27413#issuecomment-2629393189) with a repository link, hoping someone can reopen it for further investigation.

Thanks!

> **Issue description:** This issue was found while working on the Space Rocks example of the Chris Bradfield book. When the CollisionShape2D starts disabled (either in the inspector or in the _ready() method), applied_torque has no effect. Debugging shows that the torque is indeed applied but the transform matrix doesn't account for it. Forces are applied normally, though. I can thrust forward, but not rotate it.
> 
> If the CollisionShape2D starts enabled and then gets disabled (by a timer of 0.01s, for example), enabling it again works as expected (I can rotate it by applying a torque).
> 
> I didn't add this interaction in the minimal example, but if another RigidBody2D collides with the player, it is pushed back (force is applied) but no rotation is applied.
> 
> The original Space Rocks source, when imported into 3.1, suffers from this aswell. In 3.0.6 it doesn't, though.
> 
> **Minimal reproduction project:** [test.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/3004746/test.zip)
> 
> You can either disable the CollisionShape2D in the inspector or enable it and uncomment _ready() to test both cases.

 _Originally posted by @sthiago in [#27413](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/27413#issue-425040250)_

### Steps to reproduce

[Here's my repo](https://github.com/ulfben/space-rocks/tree/5f0cf1f8c6f1dd10116c71ce3c71ad4d874652ba). 

Launch the game, steer the ship (arrow keys) into an asteroid. The player goes into an INVULNERABLE state (semi-transparent), during which you remain in control (can steer) but can not shoot. 

Uncomment [line 56 in Player.gd](https://github.com/ulfben/space-rocks/blob/5f0cf1f8c6f1dd10116c71ce3c71ad4d874652ba/player.gd#L56) to disable the CollisionShape2D when INVULNERABLE. Re-launch the game and try the above again - you'll notice the player can no longer steer when INVULNERABLE. 

Or more specifically, for as long as the CollisionShape2D is disabled, the Player RidigBody2D has only thrust applied but no torque:

```
func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	constant_force = thrust	
	constant_torque = rotation_dir * spin_power
```
